title: Quarterly Commitment Mosaic: Hosted API Catalog Sprints & Overflow Strategy
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Define a repeatable quarterly planning artifact that allocates committed sprints for Hosted API + model catalog core work while preserving an overflow lane for emergent model onboarding, capacity hedging, and urgent reliability fixes. Deliverables: commitment mosaic document, sprint allocation guidelines, canary windows schedule, and a lightweight playbook for moving items between committed and overflow lanes.
problem_statement: Current quarterly plans are rigidly prescriptive and flood PM/ENG during model surge windows. This causes either missed onboarding opportunities (blocking customers) or reactive re-prioritization that increases cross-team friction and runway risk. We need a planning construct that balances a stable committed backlog with a pre-authorized overflow lane and clear decision criteria for movement.
goals: Provide a visual planning artifact (mosaic) that maps committed sprint lanes vs overflow lanes for the quarter
Reduce ad-hoc roadmap churn by 50% through defined movement criteria and pre-approved overflow capacity
Improve hosted-api model onboarding lead time from request to canary from 21 days to <=10 days for high-priority models
Ensure at least 95% of committed items complete within the quarter or receive formal roll-forward notes
success_metrics: Mean time from model onboarding request to canary <= 10 days for priority-1
Number of emergency re-prioritizations reduced by 50% vs previous quarter
Canary pass rate >= 98% for models onboarded through overflow lane

Phase 2 (weeks 3-5): Pilot overflow lane with two model onboarding requests and one reliability fix
Phase 3 (weeks 6-8): Expand to cross-org adoption; integrate overflow signals into Console alerts
Phase 4 (week 9): Post-mortem and iterate rules for next quarter
stakeholders: Engineering leads: Leah Patel (runtime), Samir Gupta (infra)
cross_team_syncs: Weekly cadence: Thurs 10:00-10:30 AM (mosaic board review)
Monthly Exec touchpoint: 1st Monday of month for commitment window sign-off
Ad-hoc: Overflow triage meetings triggered by Console 'overflow-request' tag
risks: Ambiguity in movement criteria leads to silent scope creep
Overflow lane gets overloaded and starves committed work
Capacity hedges are insufficient during an unexpected model surge
Siloed decision-making causing downstream deploy or SLA regressions
mitigation: Define explicit entry/exit criteria for overflow queue (severity, customer, capacity cost)
Reserve a hard ceiling of 12% of total sprint capacity for overflow by default
Require 'overflow approval' from runtime + infra leads for any item exceeding 8% capacity
Instrument dashboard: overflow queue length, mean time in queue, canary success rate
notes: Design pattern inspired by 'swimlane with buffer' from platform planning experiments Q3 2024
This artifact should live under Confluence: /HostedAPI/Quarterly-Mosaics
We will use the existing roadmap board in Linear with new labels 'mosaic-committed' and 'mosaic-overflow'
Consider a follow-up initiative to automate overflow gating via Console feature flags
